title: How a focus daemon decides you drifted
subtitle: Three sensors, one engine, two outputs, and a note nobody wired up

nodes.label: camera.py
nodes.simple: Watches the webcam in its own thread and reports whether a person is at the desk.

nodes.label: mic.py
nodes.simple: Reports whether the microphone is in use, so a call is not mistaken for drifting.

nodes.label: desktop.py
nodes.simple: Reports the class of the focused app and how active the desk is. Never a window title.

nodes.label: engine
nodes.simple: Takes every sensor reading and decides: focused, delegated, waiting on you or elsewhere.
nodes.deep: One asyncio loop folds presence, app class and call state into a single session state and writes a row whenever it changes.
nodes.exposes: State changes to the store and the notifier.

nodes.label: events.db
nodes.simple: The local record of every state change, written once and read by the receipt.

nodes.label: notifier
nodes.simple: Taps your phone when an agent is waiting on you.

nodes.label: NOTES.md
nodes.simple: A file that nothing else in the system reads or writes.

steps.title: The camera loses you
steps.simple: Three empty frames in a row and the sensor says nobody is at the desk.

steps.title: The engine changes state
steps.simple: Away with no call and no agent running means elsewhere.

steps.title: The change is recorded
steps.simple: One row is written so the receipt can show when you left.

whatifs.title: The camera thread dies
whatifs.change: camera.py raises and its thread exits.
whatifs.outcome: The engine keeps the last presence reading and slowly drifts to a wrong state.

quiz.q: Which part decides the session state?
quiz.why: Sensors only report readings; the engine folds them into a state.

quiz.q: Where is every state change kept?
quiz.why: events.db holds one row per state change.
